items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: we had a wonderful piano player by the name of Nat Jaffe... in that band

ctx.x: Who was in the band when you opened at the Famous Door?

Well, actually there were -- well, we had a wonderful piano player by the name of Nat Jaffe, who was -- he was like Tatum, you know. He wasn't the greatest band piano player in the world, but he had a technique like Art's. I mean he was just fantastic. And the rest of the guys in the band were -- there weren't really any stars. Bobby Burnett was in that band, a trumpet player who was with me for quite awhile after that, there, and later. And we really didn't have -- it was more or less of a team effort, rather…

singular person by the name of Johnny Mendel, not Mandel, but Johnny Mendel, out of Chicago. He was -- that wasn't his real name. He was Polish, and he was one of the sole remaining guys that knew how to growl and use a plunger. And he was in the band. And he played a particularly beautiful solo on a thing that Barney Bigard wrote, called, "Meant For a Lost Love." It's a muted solo with a harmon mute the -- it's one of the prettiest things. I still play it every now and then, when I think of it, because it's so…
